about: Evaluation set for the Ask the data agent. Every expected number has a reference SQL that tests/test_eval_cases.py runs offline. names: at least one must appear in the answer (case-insensitive). expect_sql: true = at least one successful query, false = no query, null = either. An expected number with any_of accepts any of its values, and its why says when each one is right. Tune on dev only. test was meant to be held out, but a failure in it led to a change of the notes in Step 6; test2 is the held-out split, written after the last change and run once.

cases.question: How many official Summer Olympic Games are in the data?

numbers.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT year) FROM summer_entries WHERE year <> 1906

cases.question: Which country has won the most gold medals?

numbers.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM country_medals WHERE country = 'USA' AND medal = 'Gold'

cases.name_sql: SELECT country FROM country_medals WHERE medal = 'Gold' AND country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY country ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What share of the athletes at Rio 2016 were women?

cases.question: Which country turns the largest share of its athletes into medallists?

numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN medal IS NOT NULL THEN athlete_id END) / COUNT(DISTINCT athlete_id), 1) FROM summer_entries WHERE country = 'Russia'

cases.name_sql: SELECT country FROM summer_entries WHERE country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY country HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT athlete_id) >= 1000 ORDER BY 1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN medal IS NOT NULL THEN athlete_id END) / COUNT(DISTINCT athlete_id) DESC LIMIT 1

cases.question: What share of all Olympic swimming gold medals has the USA won?

any_of.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(country = 'USA') / COUNT(*), 1) FROM country_medals WHERE medal = 'Gold' AND country IS NOT NULL AND sport = 'Swimming'
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(country = 'USA') / COUNT(*), 1) FROM country_medals WHERE medal = 'Gold' AND sport = 'Swimming'

numbers.why: Both shares are defensible. 43.9% (246 of 561) is the project's figure in findings.md: country medal tables leave out medals with no country, and Singapore's 2016 swimming gold has none (its NOC code SGP is missing from noc_regions). 43.8% (246 of 562) divides by all swimming golds, including Singapore's.

cases.question: Medallists in which sport are the tallest on average?

numbers.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(height_cm), 1) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT athlete_id, height_cm, weight_kg FROM summer_entries WHERE sport = 'Basketball' AND medal IS NOT NULL AND height_cm IS NOT NULL AND weight_kg IS NOT NULL)

cases.name_sql: SELECT sport FROM (SELECT DISTINCT athlete_id, sport, height_cm, weight_kg FROM summer_entries WHERE medal IS NOT NULL AND height_cm IS NOT NULL AND weight_kg IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY sport HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100 ORDER BY AVG(height_cm) DESC LIMIT 1
